draft.title: Why small businesses succeed or fail
card: Many small businesses close within their first few years. The reasons are often in how the owner runs the business, not only in bad luck.
Good records show what the business earns, spends, owes and is owed. The owner can then see problems early and make decisions using facts.
Cash management means keeping enough cash to pay bills on time, such as rent, wages and suppliers. A business can make a profit and still close if it runs out of cash.
Planning and market knowledge help a business last. Planning sets goals and prepares for costs. Market knowledge means knowing who the customers are and what they want.
draft.remember: Records, cash, planning and market knowledge help a business last. Poor records and cash shortages often end it.

a.q: Which situation shows a common reason a small business may close?
opts: It runs out of cash to pay its bills on time
It keeps up to date records of money in and out
It writes a plan with goals before opening
It researches what local customers want to buy
a.why: Without cash, a business cannot pay rent, wages or suppliers, even if its sales are growing. The other three are habits that help a business last.
a.clue: Which one stops the bills being paid?

b.q: Priya's bakery in Geelong sold more each month and made a profit on paper. In month eight she could not pay her flour supplier and had to close. What is the most likely reason?
opts: She did not manage her cash to meet bills when due
She did not make enough profit to stay in business
She had too much market knowledge about her customers
She kept records that were too detailed to be useful
b.why: Profit on paper does not mean cash is available when a bill is due. Priya's sales were growing, so low profit does not fit the case. Having more records or market knowledge does not cause a business to close.
b.clue: Profit and cash in the bank are not the same thing.

a.best: It runs out of cash to pay its bills on time

b.best: She did not manage her cash to meet bills when due
